prompt:
Scene:
A square-format photograph of the same two-story mall atrium, camera vantage identical to the reference image, shot with 90s direct flash. The frame now tightens implicitly on the back of the atrium where the escalator pair stands frozen mid-step. Ambient lighting is further reduced; most overheads dead, a few emergency spots glow. Slight green color cast, 35mm grain.

Subject:
The same pair of escalators rising to the second-floor balcony, with brushed-steel treads unmoving. The steel lines between treads catch the flash as parallel hotspots. The rubber handrails sit motionless. Beyond the escalators, the balcony railing and shuttered storefronts visible from the reference angle remain, but deeper in shadow. The ground floor foreground shows the edge of the terrazzo and part of the planter matching the reference vantage.

Important details:
Escalator must unambiguously read as stopped — no motion blur, no moving-step vagueness. Preserve atrium footprint, balcony rail geometry, planter location, and terrazzo pattern from the reference. Darker ambient; flash now carries more of the image. No shopper, no security, no photographer reflection on steel treads. The uncanny beat: moving-stair infrastructure that is currently not moving.

Use case:
Series image 2 of 4. Same atrium, escalator highlighted as stopped.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no people, no motion blur, no lens flare, no cinematic grade.
